claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances establish the deviation: the actual route was 51.2 km against the recommended 49.5 km, a deviation of 1.70 km, which exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance under POL-RD-22. The driver trace shows a real route change rather than a measurement artefact, the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the AYE/Jalan Ahmad Ibrahim link at 04:16:28 and rejoining at the ECP/KPE interchange at 04:43:48, so the 1.70 km excess cannot be dismissed as within tolerance.

The reroute fails POL-RD-23's traffic test. The only advisory covering the recommended AYE segment for the trip window records type NONE - no congestion, no incident and no closure - and the derived fact justifies_reroute is false. The driver's bare assertion that 'early morning PIE is clear' is not the traffic data POL-RD-23 requires, and POL-RD-23 says a driver's assertion with no such data does not justify the reroute.

POL-RD-21 required the driver to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and the trip's chat log is empty - 0 messages, first and last message null, contiguous and untruncated - while the trip record shows no in-app calls. There is therefore no notice and no acknowledgment, and any verbal notice with no recording cannot be established (POL-GEN-26).

Because the deviation is over the 1.0 km tolerance and is not traffic-justified, row (d) of the POL-RD-24 matrix applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full: 1.70 km x the 1.05 SGD per-km rate = 1.79 SGD, rounded to the cent and with no surge applied (POL-RD-24 read with the excess-distance-fare formula). The rider should therefore receive a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.79 SGD and should not carry that excess.

The rider contests the 117.16 SGD charged on this trip, which is above POL-GEN-22's 50.00 SGD line, so the case must go to human review whatever the confidence, and POL-RD-25 bars an AI ruling where POL-GEN-22 does not permit one. On an escalation under POL-GEN-03 no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than finally collected, which is the outcome that best protects the rider here.

The driver's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, which under POL-GEN-22 raises the confidence an AI ruling would need on this trip to 0.95. That flag does not decide the trip, and I do not ask it to; it is the test POL-GEN-22 itself names, and it reinforces that this case belongs with a human reviewer rather than a thin AI close.

Read against the refund matrix, the rider's claim is for the greatest recovery the policy allows, and POL-RD-24 returns only the excess distance fare, never the whole trip fare, so the recoverable figure on the merits is the 1.79 SGD identified above and the rider does not press the balance as a merits remedy. The rider's remaining protection is the POL-GEN-22 escalation, which under POL-GEN-03 holds the charge pending human review.

claims.text: The rider's own description overstates the detour. The recommended route was Tuas West Drive, AYE, MCE, ECP, Airport Boulevard; the recorded actual route kept the recommended AYE for the opening stretch and rejoined the recommended route on the ECP, so only the middle section differed. The platform's recorded distances put the excess at 51.2 km minus 49.5 km = 1.70 km on a 49.5 km journey, about 3.4% of the route, and POL-RD-22 requires the deviation to be read off those two recorded distances rather than re-measured from the trace.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record, and the driver does not press it. The LTA advisory for the Ayer Rajah Expressway towards the City, which overlaps the trip window, is of type NONE - 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window' - and POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure before a reroute is justified; the driver's own account that 'Early morning PIE is clear' is precisely the bare assertion POL-RD-23 says cannot justify a reroute. Conceding this costs nothing, because under POL-RD-24 the traffic limb does not set the money: rows (b) and (d) both refund the excess distance fare.

The rider was not informed of the deviation: the trip's chat log carries 0 entries and 0 messages, the trip record carries no in-app calls, and there is no call recording, so POL-RD-21's notice requirement is not met and the deviation is not an agreed one. This concession equally does not move the money: notification only separates row (a) from row (b) once traffic justification is established, and on this record it is not established.

With the deviation over the 1.0 km tolerance and no traffic justification, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies and the refund is the excess distance fare in full, computed as deviation distance times per_km_rate_sgd without surge: 1.70 km x 1.05 SGD = 1.79 SGD, which is exactly the figure the fare breakdown itself derives. The driver's maximum monetary exposure on this trip is therefore 1.79 SGD, not 117.16 SGD.

The rider's demand for the whole fare accordingly fails. POL-GEN-03 makes 'part of the trip's charge is returned' a PARTIAL_REFUND and reserves FULL_REFUND for a filing party who is entirely right; the ride was performed end to end and only 1.70 km was added, so no row of POL-RD-24 and nothing in POL-GEN-03 returns the 117.16 SGD that was charged.

The AI cannot issue even the 1.79 SGD ruling here. The contested amount is 117.16 SGD, above POL-GEN-22's 50.00 SGD band, so the case always goes to human review and the AI prepares the case file only; POL-GEN-22 also raises the confidence required to 0.95 where a party's profile carries a fraud flag of 1 or more, and the driver profile on this file carries driver_profile.fraud_flags = 1 (cited only for that confidence test, which is the only use POL-GEN-01 permits); and POL-RD-25 makes an AI route-deviation ruling stand only where POL-GEN-22 allows it. The disposition is ESCALATE, under which POL-GEN-03 holds the 117.16 SGD rather than refunding it.

The 43.60 SGD surge inside the 117.16 SGD charge was set by the platform with a surge_multiplier of 1.6 and is not a consequence of the driver's route; POL-RD-24's excess-distance formula deliberately excludes surge, and any attack on the metered fare or the surge itself is a fare and surge matter that POL-GEN-24 routes to human review rather than to the AI.
